belief: I have to look a certain way to be loved.
origins: Comments about weight, clothes, skin, and hair, a parent’s own struggles with appearance, school teasing, and a constant stream of edited images teach that love goes to the attractive. Dating and social pressures reinforce it. Many people spend years dieting, covering, or hiding.
teaches: God told Samuel, “Do not consider his appearance or height… the LORD does not see as man does. For man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.” Peter writes, “Your beauty should not come from outward adornment… but from the inner disposition of your heart, the unfading beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is precious in God’s sight.” Proverbs says, “Charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting.” And “God proves His love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” God’s love does not depend on appearance, and real love among people looks beyond it as well.
self_statements: No one will love me unless I look right.
I have to lose weight to be loved.
I am not attractive enough to be valued.
If I let myself go, I will be alone.
errors: Believing I am either attractive and loved or unattractive and unloved.
Insisting that I should look a certain way.
Feeling unattractive and concluding that I am unlovable.
questions: Who or what taught me that love depends on appearance?
Who loves me, and does it depend on how I look?
What qualities do I most value in the people I love?
What does God see when He looks at me?
How would I treat a friend who felt this way?
What is one way I can care for my body without punishing it?
truth: God’s love for me does not depend on appearance, and real love among people looks deeper too. I can care for my body with kindness and receive love as I am.
hw_truths: God’s love was given while I was a sinner.
A gentle spirit is precious to God.
I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
I can receive love as I am.
log: Each week, note one person who loves you as you are.
actions: Write who taught you this and what they said.
Write what you love in your friends beyond looks.
Unfollow accounts that make you feel worse.
prayer: Lord, You look at my heart. Heal the hurt of comments about my body, and help me receive love as I am and care for the body You gave me. Amen.
hw_questions: What do I value in others?
How would I treat a friend?
How can I care for myself kindly?
name_example: Sarah can write: “The Lord looks at my heart, so I am loved as I am.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “I have to look a certain way to be loved.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
